chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about drinking the juice, so he said: 'Drink it as long as it has not boiled. So when it boils, do not drink it.' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, which thing is the boiling?' He said: 'The fermentation (transformation into wine).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on drinking grape juice before and after it ferments according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the boundary between permissible fresh juice and intoxicating wine by defining 'ghalayn' as the internal fermentation process, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing *khamr* from *asir*. This hadith underscores the principle that the prohibition of wine is contingent upon the transformation of its essence rather than mere time or external signs, reflecting the Shi'a emphasis on the intrinsic properties of substances.
